title: Unity MCP bridge bound IPv6-only; clients must dial 127.0.0.1, not localhost
content: Unity's MCP bridge (com.unity.mcp-server) creates its HttpListener with the single prefix 'http://localhost:8090/'. On this machine http.sys registers that as IPv6-only, so netstat shows only '[::1]:8090 LISTENING'. Consequences: (1) any client that dials 127.0.0.1 gets connection-refused; (2) Node's fetch resolves 'localhost' to [::1] first, and when the IPv6 connect is unavailable it falls back to IPv4 but keeps the Host header 'localhost:8090', which the IPv4 endpoint answers with '400 Bad Request (Invalid host)'. The Node bridge reported this misleadingly as 'Failed to connect to Unity after 3 attempts'. Fix applied in both places: McpUnityServer.StartServer() now also registers 'http://127.0.0.1:{port}/' (with a fallback to the localhost-only prefix if http.sys refuses it), and the Node client dials UNITY_HOST (default 127.0.0.1) instead of hardcoded localhost. Verified: fetch to http://127.0.0.1:8090 returns 200 and tools execute. Diagnostic shortcut: POST {"id":"x","type":"request","method":"project.getInfo"} to the bridge with Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing to separate Unity-side health from client-side connectivity.
